title: Example annotated photo and site map
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Physical fieldwork enquiry (Paper 1 Section B)
source: Written for geography/y10 lesson 67 (Example annotated photo and site map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 67: Presenting data: annotated photos, maps and field sketches. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

box.title: Stick or sketch your photo here, then add three annotations (describe, explain, link)

parts.text: Link: slower infiltration than thick grass

keywords.def: a word or phrase naming a feature
a note that explains or describes a feature
photos, sketches and maps used as proof

questions.q: Turn this label into an annotation: 'drain'.
questions.a: For example: drain at the lowest point; run-off from the patio flows here

questions.q: Why mark sampling points on a map?
questions.a: To show where data came from and allow comparison

questions.q: Give one strength of photos as evidence.
questions.a: Show real conditions, can be checked by others

questions.q: Core: Annotate two of your photos (three annotations each) and make an annotated site map with sampling points and mean times.
questions.a: Accurate annotations that describe and explain; clear map with data

questions.q: Extend: (4 marks, own exam-style) Explain how one visual method helped you reach a conclusion.
questions.a: Named method, what it showed, link to hypothesis, why numbers alone were not enough

questions.q: Stretch: How could a GIS map improve your presentation?
questions.a: Geolocate points, overlay flood risk layers, show patterns over a wider area

options: Gravel: loose stones; water drained in 75 s
questions.a: B) Gravel: loose stones; water drained in 75 s. An annotation describes or explains; the others only name.

questions.q: Big question: what can a photo prove that a graph cannot?
questions.a: Why results happened: conditions such as compaction or slope
